title: Port inspector
blurb: Runs 13 live IDL and runtime checks across both ends of the shared channel: prototype accessor descriptor, MessagePort identity, per-BaseAudioContext isolation, strict-mode readonly enforcement, and AudioWorkletGlobalScope introspection.
question: Do both AudioWorklet.prototype.port and AudioWorkletGlobalScope.prototype.port expose readonly prototype accessors returning one stable MessagePort per BaseAudioContext?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, the inspector recorded 0 pass, 8 fail on the main-thread IDL checks, and 5 not reachable on the global-scope checks because no shared channel exists in that engine. Spec path not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (unsupported branch verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Assigning ctx.audioWorklet.port = null in strict mode creates an own property instead of throwing TypeError on engines without the getter
friction.repro: Run 'use strict'; ctx.audioWorklet.port = null on a browser lacking AudioWorklet.prototype.port (such as Chrome 153 or Safari); no TypeError is thrown and a.audioWorklet.port becomes null.
friction.workaround: Feature-detect with 'port' in AudioWorklet.prototype and check instanceof MessagePort before using or testing the attribute.
